source_text: Quae cum ita sint, primum sciendum est, quoniam de diuinatione daemonum quaestio est, illos ea plerumque praenuntiare, quae ipsi facturi sunt. accipiunt enim saepe potestatem et morbos inmittere et ipsum aerem uitiando morbidum reddere et peruersis atque amatoribus terrenorum commodorum malefacta suadere, de quorum moribus certi sunt, quod sint eis talia suadentibus consensuri. suadent autem miris et inuisibilibus modis per illam subtilitatem corporum suorum corpora hominum non sentientium penetrando et se cogitationibus eorum per quaedam imaginaria uisa miscendo, siue uigilantium siue dormientium. aliquando autem non quae ipsi faciunt, sed quae naturalibus signis futura praenoscunt, quae signa in hominum sensus uenire non possunt, ante praedicunt. neque enim quia praeuidet medicus, quod non praeuidet eius artis ignarus, ideo iam diuinus habendus est. quid autem mirum, si quemadmodum ille in corporis humani uel perturbata uel modificata temperie seu bonas seu malas futuras praeuidet ualitudines, sic daemon in aeris affectione atque ordinatione sibi nota, nobis ignota futuras praeuidet tempestates\'? aliquando et hominum dispositiones non solum uoce prolatas, uerum etiam cogitatione conceptas, cura signa quaedam ex animo exprimuntur in corpore, tota facilitate perdiscunt atque hinc etiam multa futura praenuntiant, aliis uidelicet mira, qui ista disposita non nouerunt. sicut enim adparet concitatior animi motus in uultu, ut ab hominibus quoque aliquid forinsecus agnoscatur, quod intrinsecus agitur, ita non debet esse incredibile, si etiam leniores cogitationes dant aliqua signa per corpus, quae obtuso sensu hominum cognosci non possunt, acuto autem daemonum possunt.
thought_title: How demons predict what they themselves will do or read from signs
orientation: Augustine is explaining the natural limits and methods of demonic divination, after arguing that demons' bodily abilities do not make them superior to good humans.
pass_a_gloss: Since these things are so, first it must be known, because the question is about the divination of demons, that they generally foretell those things which they themselves are going to do. For they often receive power both to send diseases and to make the air itself diseased by corrupting it and to persuade wicked deeds to perverse men and lovers of earthly advantages, about whose character they are certain that they will agree to such things when they persuade them. But they persuade by wonderful and invisible methods, through that fineness of their bodies, penetrating the bodies of men who do not perceive it and mixing themselves into their thoughts through certain imaginary visions, whether of those awake or of those sleeping. But sometimes they predict beforehand not the things which they themselves do, but the things which they know beforehand as future by natural signs, which signs cannot come into the senses of men. For it is not the case that because a physician foresees what one ignorant of his art does not foresee, therefore he must already be considered a diviner. But what is wonderful, if just as that one in the disturbed or modified condition of the human body foresees future health, whether good or bad, so a demon in the condition and ordering of the air, known to itself, unknown to us, foresees future storms? Sometimes they also learn with complete ease the dispositions of men, not only those uttered by voice, but even those conceived in thought, when certain signs from the mind are expressed in the body, and from this they also foretell many future things, which are of course wonderful to others, who have not known these things as arranged. For just as a rather agitated motion of the mind appears in the face, so that by men too something is recognized outwardly which is done inwardly, so it ought not to be incredible, if even gentler thoughts give some signs through the body, which cannot be known by the dull sense of men, but can be known by the keen sense of demons.

choices.english: to perverse men and lovers of earthly advantages
choices.why: The dative plural marks the indirect object of suadere: demons persuade wicked deeds to these people, not that these people are the ones doing the persuading.
rejected: perverse men who love earthly advantages

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for the demons' subtle bodily nature.
The adjective is used substantivally here to mean one who has divine foreknowledge, matching the treatise's contrast between divination and natural foresight.
Refers to the bodily state or balance, rendered plainly to keep the medical analogy clear.
Keeps the sense of images presented to the mind, whether waking or sleeping, without importing a technical term.
Ablative of manner emphasizing the demons' effortless perception, matching the argument that this is a natural advantage, not divine power.

pass_b_english: Since this is so, the first thing to understand—because the question is about the divination of demons—is that they usually foretell what they themselves are going to do. They often receive power to send diseases, to make the air itself unhealthy by corrupting it, and to persuade wicked deeds to perverse lovers of earthly advantages, men whose character they know for certain will consent to such persuasion. They persuade in astonishing and invisible ways, penetrating the bodies of unaware people through the subtlety of their own bodies and mixing themselves into their thoughts through certain imaginary visions, whether they are awake or asleep.

Sometimes, however, they predict not what they themselves will do but what they know beforehand from natural signs—signs that cannot reach human senses. A physician foresees what someone ignorant of his art does not foresee, but that does not make him a diviner. What is remarkable if, just as the physician foresees future good or bad health in the disturbed or balanced condition of the human body, so the demon foresees future storms in the state and ordering of the air, which is known to him and unknown to us?

Sometimes they also learn with complete ease the dispositions of human beings—not only those spoken aloud but even those conceived in thought—since certain signs from the mind are expressed in the body, and from this they foretell many future things that seem astonishing to others who do not know these dispositions. Just as a more agitated movement of the mind appears in the face, so that even other people recognize outwardly what is happening inwardly, so it should not be incredible that even gentler thoughts give some signs through the body, signs that cannot be known by the dull senses of human beings but can be known by the keen senses of demons.

problems.quote: to persuade wicked deeds to perverse men who are lovers of earthly advantages
problems.source_quote: peruersis atque amatoribus terrenorum commodorum malefacta suadere
problems.why: Latin 'peruersis' and 'amatoribus' are datives parallel to each other, both modified by 'terrenorum commodorum': 'to perverse men and lovers of earthly advantages'. English makes 'perverse men who are lovers' a single group, losing that demons target both the perverse and those who love earthly goods.
problems.fix: to persuade wicked deeds to perverse men and to lovers of earthly advantages

edits.old: to persuade wicked deeds to perverse men who are lovers of earthly advantages
edits.new: to persuade wicked deeds to perverse men and to lovers of earthly advantages

fixed: Changed 'perverse men who are lovers of earthly advantages' to 'perverse men and to lovers of earthly advantages' because the Latin 'peruersis atque amatoribus terrenorum commodorum' has two parallel datives, both governed by 'suadere'.

problems.quote: perverse men and to lovers of earthly advantages
problems.why: Latin 'peruersis' is dative plural adjective modifying 'amatoribus', not a separate noun 'men'.
problems.fix: to perverse lovers of earthly advantages

problems.quote: when certain signs from the mind are expressed in the body
problems.source_quote: cura signa quaedam ex animo exprimuntur in corpore
problems.why: 'cura' means 'because' or 'since', not 'when'; causal not temporal.
problems.fix: since certain signs from the mind are expressed in the body
problems.ruling: 'cura' = 'because/since' (causal), mistranslated as 'when' (temporal), changing logical relationship of clause.

edits.old: to perverse men and to lovers of earthly advantages
edits.new: to perverse lovers of earthly advantages

edits.old: when certain signs from the mind are expressed in the body
edits.new: since certain signs from the mind are expressed in the body

fixed: Changed 'perverse men and to lovers of earthly advantages' to 'perverse lovers of earthly advantages' because 'peruersis' is a dative plural adjective modifying 'amatoribus', not a separate noun.
Changed 'when certain signs' to 'since certain signs' because 'cura' is causal, not temporal.

last_rejected.why: Latin 'peruersis' is dative plural modifying people, not adjective for 'lovers'; means 'to perverse men and to lovers'
last_rejected.fix: to perverse men and lovers of earthly advantages
last_rejected.ruling: 'peruersis atque amatoribus' are coordinate datives; 'perverse lovers of earthly advantages' captures the sense adequately.

last_rejected.quote: men whose character they know for certain will consent
last_rejected.source_quote: de quorum moribus certi sunt, quod sint eis talia suadentibus consensuri
last_rejected.why: Missing 'de quorum moribus certi sunt' (they are certain about whose character); relative clause misattached
last_rejected.fix: men about whose character they are certain, who will consent when such things are urged on them
last_rejected.ruling: 'whose character they know for certain will consent' does render 'de quorum moribus certi sunt'; awkward but meaning is present.

last_rejected.quote: whether they are awake or asleep
last_rejected.why: Latin genitive plurals modify 'hominum' understood; 'they' wrongly implies demons not humans
last_rejected.fix: whether of those awake or of those asleep
last_rejected.ruling: 'siue uigilantium siue dormientium' agrees with 'hominum'; 'they' refers to people in context, not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: which is known to him and unknown to us
last_rejected.why: Latin 'sibi' refers to demons (plural), not singular 'the demon'; pronoun error
last_rejected.fix: which is known to them and unknown to us
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'daemon' can be singular collective; 'him' vs 'them' is minor pronoun agreement, not meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: since certain signs from the mind are expressed in the body
last_rejected.source_quote: cura signa quaedam ex animo exprimuntur in corpore
last_rejected.why: Latin 'cura' means 'because' (causal conjunction), not 'since' temporal; also 'cura' is archaic/quasi-prepositional 'by care/attention'
last_rejected.fix: because by care certain signs are expressed from mind in body
last_rejected.ruling: 'cura' is causal conjunction 'because/since'; translator's 'since' renders it correctly; no real error.
